newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha strong on prompt supply conundrum.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha strong on prompt supply conundrum.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices remained firm on continued bidding in the physical market, while end-users complained that neither the prices nor the crack spreads were justified.
Tracking a modest rebound in crude oil prices, Feb swaps rose $4 to $223/$224 a tonne and March tacked on the same amount to $213/$214, sources said.
End-users and brokers said three traders still appeared to be short material for this month, but details on nominations were only known by them, creating more uncertainty in the market.
Their bids for specific size and quality were boosting physical prices, though total supplies were seen as ample and smaller material was priced at a discount, sources said.
Cargoes were notionally assessed at $218/$228 cif, up $2 from Monday, with the wide range caused by the varied prices for sizes and specifications.
Two traders were expected to bid for pipeline spec and another in the paper market.
One source said a trader was bidding in the high $220s against $229 for pipeline spec.
"There is enough material in the right quality but it does not fit the bids from the traders," he said. "These bids are not from this world...These numbers do not reflect the supply and demand."
He guessed that the traders were long the swaps between 100,000 and 200,000 tonnes, so any losses due to high physical prices would be offset by gains in the swaps.
The strong prompt market was underscored by continued strength in the spread between physical naphtha and front-month Brent crude--which has held at 5-1/2 year highs between $60 and $70 a tonne.
Sources speculated that one trader was short 25,000 tonnes to be delivered by February 17th, with the exact nomination day unsure.
Another trader was seen short 25,000 tonnes and third trader short two lots of 25,000 tonnes, both traders to deliver by the end of the month.
One source said he had open spec material of 25,000 tonnes that he would sell at $215/$220, but the traders wanted pipeline spec material of 25,000 tonnes and in one lot.
Trading was expected to heat up later in the afternoon when price quotations were set.
